preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 2^16 inclusive.
There are exactly n pairs of degree and XOR sum values provided.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= d <= n - 1 for d in degrees) and all(0 <= s < 2**16 for s in xor_sums)
preconditions.description: Each degree is between 0 and n-1, and each XOR sum is between 0 and 2^16 - 1.
It is guaranteed that a valid forest exists corresponding to the input data.

postconditions.description: The number of edges printed matches the count m.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n and u != v for u, v in edges)
postconditions.description: Every edge connects two distinct valid vertices within the range [0, n-1].

postconditions.expression: len(edges) == len(set(edges)) and len(edges) == len(set(tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges))
postconditions.description: No duplicate edges exist in the output (considering undirected nature).

postconditions.expression: all(sum(1 for u, v in edges if u == i or v == i) == degrees[i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For every vertex i, the number of incident edges in the output equals the input degree_i.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda i: 0 if degrees[i] == 0 else functools.reduce(lambda x, y: x ^ y, [u if u != i else v for u, v in edges if u == i or v == i])) == xor_sums[i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For every vertex i, the XOR sum of its neighbors in the output equals the input s_i.
The graph is a forest (acyclic), where the number of edges equals n minus the number of connected components (roots).
